assertion_analysis.failure_condition_and_regression: Leaving the member live, selecting the permanent identity, or failing the mutable write prevents this literal identity result.
Removing the mutable increment fails fixture version 7 plus one.
Returning a refused or unsuccessful production gate receipt fails this literal success check.
Returning the auxiliary version instead of the incremented aggregate version fails the second independent literal expectation.
Not persisting either aggregate update fails the independently read file-envelope version.

Dropping or corrupting the mocked gate result when persisting the run fails the fresh aggregate read; report is supplied fixture data, but the observed side is independently read persistence, not the mock return compared with itself.
Copying projected store membership into the aggregate fails registration and reap cases against the pre-mutation file snapshot.
Copying projected store holds into the aggregate fails the hold case against the pre-mutation file snapshot.
Reimporting stale aggregate collections or changing the mutable version during aggregate updates fails the independently captured pre-update store snapshot.
Returning the store version from load restores the prior defect and fails this literal expectation.
Omitting the projection marker or returning the aggregate version for it fails the literal store-version expectation.
Restoring ledger.load as the roster version source at routing.py:3476 supplies file version 9 to store version 8 and refuses instead of returning the literal reaped identity.
Removing the stale aggregate version guard accepts version 7 after file version 9 and fails pytest.raises.

assertion_independence: Supplied gate report is checked through an independent aggregate read; captured aggregate/store snapshots test preservation. No added assertion compares a mock return directly with its own supplied value. Version expectations are fixture-derived literals, not writer-return values.
